## Claims
- [source-backed] The two Theorem 5.4 families are \(\{s_\mu: i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 18-33]
- [computed] For \(i=j=p=2,c=5\), task 132’s exact integral Pieri/Smith computation establishes \(J_{2,5}/\Lambda_+J_{2,5}\cong\mathbb Z^6\), torsion-free. [artifact 189fc5f912d5ce0d7f385f5f68873379380542c3b14807b48344196febd2a397]
- [proved] Here \(r=7,q=4,n=11\), hence \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=2\), and \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}=6\). The accepted generating families specialize to
  \[
  \mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},
  \quad
  \mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
  \]
  Since either accepted six-element family generates \(J_{2,5}\), its images surject \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J_{2,5}/\Lambda_+J_{2,5}\cong\mathbb Z^6\). This surjection is unimodular, so the images are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. A proper subfamily cannot generate the quotient and therefore cannot generate \(J_{2,5}\). Thus both families are minimal generating sets.
